simple.meaning: סֹלְלָה (çôlᵉlâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a military mound , i.e. rampart of besiegers.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 11 times in 2 Samuel, 2 Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and 1 more, beginning at 2 Samuel 20:15. The surrounding contexts include kingship, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סֹלְלָה (H5550) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סֹלְלָה (çôlᵉlâh) / H5550 is traced through 2 Samuel 20:15, 2 Kings 19:32, Isaiah 37:33, Jeremiah 6:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: They came and besieged him in Abel of Beth Maacah, and they cast up a mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart; and all the people who were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
“Therefore Yahweh says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there. He will not come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.
“Therefore Yahweh says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.
For Yahweh of Armies said, “Cut down trees, and cast up a mound against Jerusalem. This is the city to be visited. She is wholly oppression within herself.

“Behold, siege ramps have come to the city to take it. The city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword, of the famine, and of the pestilence. What you have spoken has happened. Behold, you see it.

For Yahweh, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah, which are broken down to make a defense against the mounds and against the sword;
Lay siege against it, build forts against it, and cast up a mound against it. Also set camps against it and plant battering rams against it all around.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company won’t help him in the war, when they cast up mounds and build forts, to cut off many persons.
I will overturn, overturn, overturn it. This also will be no more, until he comes whose right it is; and I will give it.” ’
He will kill your daughters in the field with the sword. He will make forts against you, cast up a mound against you, and raise up the buckler against you.

So the king of the north will come and cast up a mound, and take a well-fortified city. The forces of the south won’t stand, neither will his chosen people, neither will there be any strength to stand.

definitions.short: a military mound , i.e. rampart of besiegers
definitions.full: H5550. solelah סֹלְלָה noun feminine mound ; — ׳ס 2Sam 20:15 7 t.; סוֺלְלָה Dan 11:15 ; plural סֹלְלוֺת Jer 32:24 ; 33:4 . — עַלהָֿעִיר ס ׳שָׁפַךְ cast up mound against the city , besieging it, 2Kin 19:32 = Isa 37:33 ; Jer 6:6 ; Ezek 4:2 ; 26:8 ; with אֶל 2Sam 20:15 (error for על ); without העיר על Ezek 17:17 ; 21:17 ; Dan 11:15 without verb Jer 32:24 ; 33:4 .
definitions.rootNote: or סוֹלְלָה ; active participle feminine of 5549 , but used passively;
